note: Market model inputs. Every figure carries a provenance entry: 'verified' read from the entity's own page on the date given; 'assumption' has no source and is Frank's to set. Frank's rulings 8 Sep 2026: six English-first countries are the launch market, every other country is uncounted upside; NIH-hosted research counts as a source; undiagnosed people are an uncounted upside, not a multiplier.

countries.us.note: Census Bureau national population by single year of age, NC-EST2024, vintage 2024: total 340,110,988; 13 and over 288,872,301; 13 to 17 21,894,033. Read 8 Sep 2026.

countries.uk.note: ONS mid-2024 estimates file (mye24tablesuk.xlsx, MYE2 Persons by single year of age): all ages 69,281,437; 13 and over 59,222,071 (85.5%). Read 8 Sep 2026.

countries.ca.note: Statistics Canada, The Daily, 24 Sep 2025: population 41,651,653 on 1 July 2025; 0 to 14 is 15.0%. The figure used is 15 and over, 85.0%; 13 and 14 year olds are not added because the single-age table renders only in a browser, so the count is slightly low.

countries.au.note: Australian Bureau of Statistics, National, state and territory population, table 59, population by single year of age, June 2025: all ages 27,611,026; 13 and over 23,482,317 (85.1%). Read 8 Sep 2026. The December 2025 headline total is 27,801,023.

countries.nz.note: Stats NZ, 5,324,700 at 30 June 2025. Read 8 Sep 2026. The age split is not in hand: the release's tables render only in a browser, so the 85% placeholder share applies to New Zealand alone.

countries.ie.note: Central Statistics Office data service, table PEA01, April 2026 estimate: all ages 5,525,600; 15 and over 4,533,200; 10 to 14 377,100. 13 and over taken as 15 and over plus two fifths of 10 to 14, 4,684,040 (84.8%). Read 8 Sep 2026.

shares.age13plusOutsideUS.note: Share aged 13 and over where a country's own age table is not in hand. After 8 Sep this applies only to New Zealand. The four countries with their own tables came out at 85.5% (UK), 85.0% (Canada, 15 and over), 85.1% (Australia) and 84.8% (Ireland), so the placeholder is in line.

prevalence.autismAdultRate.note: WHO autism fact sheet: in 2021 about 1 in 127 persons worldwide had autism. Applied to everyone 18 and over, and to 13 to 17 outside the US.

prevalence.autismTeenUSRate.note: CDC ADDM Network: about 1 in 31 children aged 8 identified with autism (2022). Applying an 8-year-old rate to 13 to 17 year olds is an assumption; it is the only US rate CDC publishes for children.

prevalence.minimallyVerbalShare.note: Tager-Flusberg and Kasari 2013, NIH-hosted (PMC3869868): about 30% of children with autism remain minimally verbal even after years of intervention. Applied to adults as well, which is an assumption; the study is about school-aged children.

prevalence.aphasiaUS.note: NIDCD (NIH): about 2 million people in the United States have aphasia, nearly 180,000 acquire it each year. The same rate per head is applied to the other five countries, which is an assumption. Stroke survivors are not counted separately, because aphasia is the speech-loss part of stroke and counting both would double count.

schools.usIdeaAutism.note: NCES Digest table 204.30, 2022-23: 980,000 served under the autism category ages 3 to 21 (13.0%). Shown for scale; the count used is the 2024-25 federal file's 13 through 21 line.

schools.usRegularDistricts.note: NCES Digest table 214.30: 13,349 regular public school districts in 2019-20.

schools.englandEhcPlans.note: Department for Education headline, 2025/26: 538,547 pupils with an EHC plan (6.0%), autism the most common primary need (33.5%). Shown for scale; the count used is the autism-by-age line.

schools.seatsPerDistrict.note: Average seats in a district order. Nobody has sold one yet.

clinical.usInpatientRehabFacilities.note: CMS Provider Data Catalog, Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility general information dataset: 1,222 Medicare-certified facilities, 8 Sep 2026. Outpatient speech therapy practices, ALS clinics and the other four countries' rehab centers are not counted: the US labor statistics page for speech-language pathologists blocked the request and ASHA's site answers with a bot challenge.

clinical.seatsPerFacility.note: Seats a facility buys. Nobody has sold one yet.

conversion.note: Frank's to set. Buyer share is new one-time buyers each year as a share of the counted consumer market; subscription attach is the share of all buyers to date who hold the Family Tether at year end; school seat share is new seats each year as a share of the counted school market; clinic facility share is the share of facilities that have bought by that year, times seats per facility. Base is roughly twice the pasted hub's ramp in Year 1 as a share of market; Low is half of Base; High is twice Base.

opex.note: Operating expenses per year are the Ceiling case in Frank's 7 Sep document, the closest in scale.

stores.note: Google Play: paid apps, in-app purchases and subscriptions in all six countries (Google's supported locations page, 15 Dec 2025 version, pasted by Frank 8 Sep 2026). Apple: all six are App Store countries or regions with English as the default store language (App Store Connect reference, App Store localizations, pasted by Frank 8 Sep 2026). The same Apple list shows English (U.K.) as the default store language in India, Nigeria, the Philippines, South Africa, Singapore and most of Africa and the Caribbean, which is the uncounted upside.
